transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah… so, I’m here because things at work kind of went off the rails, and I’m having a hard time explaining it in a way that doesn’t sound reckless.

I work in HR, and I was leading this onboarding launch, and I pushed it forward before all the approvals were actually in place. I committed company money, got vendors moving, took up their time, made promises basically—because in the moment it felt like the right move. It felt bold, honestly, and necessary, like if I didn’t drive it forward then it was going to get stuck in bureaucracy and lose momentum.

But now, looking back, I can see that I got way out ahead of everyone. I’m on leave now, and people keep asking me what I was thinking, and I don’t really have a clean answer that satisfies them. At the time it made total sense to me. Now it feels painful and embarrassing, and I’m here because I need to understand what happened.
During the time you were pushing this project ahead, were you sleeping much less than usual without feeling tired?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that cleanly. I mean, I wasn’t exactly tracking my sleep in a structured way or anything, and that whole period feels a little blurred together now because I was so focused on the launch and the approvals and the vendor timelines.

I don’t want to say, “Yes, definitely,” if that makes it sound like I know for sure. There were nights where I stayed up later than I probably should have, because I was thinking through pieces of the project or responding to things, but whether I was sleeping much less than usual and not feeling tired… I don’t know. I guess I didn’t stop and notice it at the time. I was just kind of pushing through and assuming it was normal work pressure.
During that period, did you feel unusually high, euphoric, or intensely energized?

Yeah… I think that’s probably fair to say, though I don’t know if I would have called it “euphoric” at the time.

For the past few weeks, I had these stretches where I felt almost brilliantly alive, like everything finally made sense and I could see exactly what HR should be doing, and I was the only one willing to actually move it forward. It felt like I could finally show leadership what HR can be, not just paperwork and compliance and waiting for six people to sign off on something obvious. There was this intensity to it, like I was charged up and clear and confident.

But it wasn’t only positive. If someone questioned me—even about something small, like edits to the rollout materials or routine budget questions—I could get furious really fast. Not just annoyed, but like, “Why are you slowing this down? Why can’t you see the bigger picture?” And looking back, some of those questions were normal. They weren’t attacking me. But in the moment they felt insulting or obstructive, and I reacted like people were getting in the way of something important. So… yes, energized, definitely. High in a way, sometimes. And also very irritable.
During that time, did you need much less sleep than usual and still feel rested?

I’m not sure. I know that’s probably frustrating because it sounds like a yes-or-no thing, but I really don’t have a clean record of it in my head.

I wasn’t going to bed thinking, “Wow, I only need four hours now,” or anything that clear. I remember being very absorbed in work and not paying much attention to normal routines, and there were definitely nights where sleep felt like less of a priority because I had one more email to send or one more plan to think through. But whether I truly needed much less sleep and still felt rested… I don’t know.

At the time, I don’t think I was checking in with myself that way. I was just moving. If I felt awake, I assumed it was because the work was urgent or important, not because anything unusual was happening with me. Looking back, it’s hard to separate being keyed up and focused from actually being rested. So I guess my honest answer is: I may have been sleeping less at points, but I can’t confidently say I needed less sleep or felt rested from it.
During that period, did you have any beliefs that others said were unrealistic or not true, even though they felt completely true to you?

I don’t know that I had anything like that, exactly. I mean, I definitely felt very strongly about what I was doing, and I’m sure other people thought I was overestimating things or being too convinced that my approach was right. But in terms of a belief where someone said, “That’s not true,” and I still felt completely certain despite that… I’m not sure.

It’s hard because at work people disagree all the time, and someone can say, “That timeline isn’t realistic,” or “Leadership isn’t going to approve that,” and in the moment I might have thought they were being overly cautious or not understanding the urgency. But that feels different from believing something that was just flat-out not real. I don’t remember anyone confronting me like, “That isn’t happening,” or “That’s not based in reality.”

So… I guess my answer would be no, not that I’m aware of. Or at least nothing that stands out to me as a belief like that.
About how many days in a row did that unusually energized, confident, or irritable state last?

It’s been… I’d say about a month, roughly. Not every single minute of every day at the exact same intensity, but the overall state—being really keyed up, confident, easily irritated, feeling like I had to push things forward—has been building for about a month now.

It started around when the new executive came in and started challenging the onboarding redesign I’d been working on. At first I told myself it was just normal pressure, like, okay, someone new is asking questions and I need to defend the work. But then it kind of kept ramping up. I got more and more focused on proving the redesign was right, and every objection felt bigger than it probably was.

So if you’re asking how many days in a row, I’d say it’s been about four weeks, give or take. The intensity has fluctuated, but I don’t think it really went away during that time.
Did this period lead to serious problems in your functioning, such as being put on leave from work?

Yes. I mean… that’s the part that’s hardest to say out loud, because it’s not just that things got tense or I had a bad week at work. It did become serious.

Because of how I handled the launch and the conflicts around it, I’ve been put on administrative leave. And I’m no longer being trusted to manage the HR projects I was leading, which is… honestly, humiliating and kind of devastating, because those projects were my responsibility and I thought I was protecting them. At the time I felt like I was pushing things forward and doing what needed to be done, but the way it played out made people lose confidence in me.

So yes, it affected my functioning in a real way. It wasn’t just internal stress or people being annoyed with me. There were consequences. I’m not currently in control of the work I was supposed to be leading.
Before this started, had you been diagnosed with any medical condition that affected your brain or hormones, like a thyroid problem, seizures, a head injury, or a neurological illness?

Not that I know of. I mean, I’ve never been told I have anything like that affecting my brain or hormones.

I’m trying to think carefully, because I don’t want to just give you a quick no if there’s something I’m forgetting, but… no, I don’t have a history of seizures or a head injury or some neurological illness that I’m aware of. And I haven’t been diagnosed with a thyroid problem, at least not that anyone has told me.

I’ve had normal life stress and work stress and all of that, but in terms of an actual medical condition that would explain this kind of change, I don’t know of one.
Before this started, had you started using any drugs or medications that seemed to affect your mood or energy?

I don’t think so. I’m trying to think through it because I know that’s important, but I can’t point to any new drug or medication that started right before this and then suddenly my mood or energy changed.

I wasn’t, like… experimenting with anything, at least not in a way that I connect to this. And I don’t remember starting some new prescription or supplement and then feeling different because of it. It feels more like everything escalated around the work situation, not like I took something and then became this way.

So, no—not that I’m aware of. If there’s something specific you’re wondering about, I can try to remember more carefully, but nothing obvious comes to mind.
During this period, were you hospitalized for your mood or behavior?

No, I wasn’t hospitalized. At least, not admitted to a hospital or anything like that.

There were definitely consequences, like the leave from work, and people around me were concerned, but it didn’t get to the point where I was taken to an ER or kept inpatient somewhere for my mood or behavior. I guess I’m a little embarrassed even answering it, because the question makes it sound very serious—and it was serious in its own way—but no, there wasn’t a hospitalization.
Before this past month, have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day or lost interest in almost everything?

I’m not really sure how to answer that cleanly. I mean, I’ve had stretches where I felt down, or discouraged, or kind of burned out, like anyone does, but I don’t know that I’d say there was a clear two-week period before this past month where I was depressed most of the day nearly every day.

And the “lost interest in almost everything” part… I don’t think so. Not in a way that stands out to me as, like, a distinct episode. I can remember being tired of work or not wanting to deal with certain things, but that feels different from losing interest in everything.

So I guess my answer is: not that I can clearly identify. If it happened, I don’t have a specific period in mind that I’d point to and say yes, that was definitely that.
Before this past month, had you ever gone through a period when you felt depressed nearly every day for at least two weeks?

I’m not sure I can say yes to that. I know I’ve had times before where I felt low or worn down, especially if things were stressful, but when you say “nearly every day for at least two weeks,” I don’t have a clear memory of a period like that.

It’s hard because I don’t want to accidentally minimize something, but I also don’t want to label normal rough patches as something more than they were. I can remember being unhappy or frustrated at different points, but not this sustained, day-after-day depressed feeling for two weeks that really stands out to me. So… no, not that I can clearly identify before this past month.
Before this past month, had you ever had a period when you felt unusually energized, confident, or irritable like this?

Before this past month? I don’t think so, not like this. I mean, I’ve definitely had times in my life where I felt motivated or confident at work, or where I got irritated with people, but this felt… different in intensity.

These past few weeks, it’s been like I’ll feel brilliantly alive, almost like everything suddenly makes sense and I can finally show leadership what HR is supposed to be—like I can see all the problems and all the solutions at once. And then if someone questions me, even about something small, like edits to something I wrote or a routine budget question, I can get furious really fast. Not just annoyed, but like, “How are you not seeing what I’m seeing?”

Before this month, I don’t remember having that same kind of swing between feeling that energized and confident and then suddenly intensely irritated. I’ve had normal stress or ambition, sure, but not this version of it.

And the “lost interest in almost everything” part… I don’t think so. Not in a way that stands out to me as, like, a distinct episode. I can remember being tired of work or not wanting to deal with certain things, but that feels different from losing interest in everything.

So I guess my answer is: not that I can clearly identify. If it happened, I don’t have a specific period in mind that I’d point to and say yes, that was definitely that.

patient.answer:
Before this past month? I don’t think so, not like this. I mean, I’ve definitely had times in my life where I felt motivated or confident at work, or where I got irritated with people, but this felt… different in intensity.

These past few weeks, it’s been like I’ll feel brilliantly alive, almost like everything suddenly makes sense and I can finally show leadership what HR is supposed to be—like I can see all the problems and all the solutions at once. And then if someone questions me, even about something small, like edits to something I wrote or a routine budget question, I can get furious really fast. Not just annoyed, but like, “How are you not seeing what I’m seeing?”

Before this month, I don’t remember having that same kind of swing between feeling that energized and confident and then suddenly intensely irritated. I’ve had normal stress or ambition, sure, but not this version of it.
